title: Parts of an Old-Fashioned Window
description: Explore a framed window through its movable sections, dividing strips, and surrounding woodwork.
cardDescription: Explore a framed window through its movable sections, dividing strips, and surrounding woodwork.
focus: A window’s glass, moving sash, and surrounding frame have different names. The clues distinguish small dividing strips from the larger structural pieces around the opening.
solvingTip: Use the location: beneath the glass, beside the opening, or between separate panes.
words: Frame holding window glass, often movable within a larger frame
Vertical member dividing adjacent window units or large sections
Narrow strip separating small panes within a window sash
Horizontal ledge at the bottom of a window opening
Horizontal structural support above a window opening
Vertical side of a window's surrounding opening
Single sheet of glass set into a window
Transparent material filling most ordinary window openings
Small fastening keeping a window section closed
Joint allowing a casement window to swing
Outer support surrounding the window assembly
Window style with a sash hinged at the side
To fit a window with its glass
Horizontal member within a framed window sash

answerNotes.SASH: A sash holds the glazing; the surrounding window frame supports the whole assembly.
answerNotes.MULLION: A mullion separates larger sections, while a muntin divides smaller panes within a sash.
answerNotes.MUNTIN: Muntins divide individual panes; the word differs from mullion despite the similar sound.
answerNotes.SILL: The sill is at the bottom, while the lintel is above the opening.
answerNotes.LINTEL: A lintel carries loads over the opening rather than supporting flowerpots below it.

title: A Door Lock and Its Fittings
description: Identify the visible parts and common mechanism names around a household door lock.
cardDescription: Identify the visible parts and common mechanism names around a household door lock.
subtheme: A Door Lock and Its Fittings
focus: The clues separate the moving fastening piece from the plate receiving it and from the trim around the key opening. They name components rather than describing lock-opening techniques.
solvingTip: Use which part moves and which stays fixed in the doorway.
words: Door-fastening bolt that does not spring back like an ordinary latch
Fastening piece that commonly catches automatically when a door closes
Fixed door-frame plate receiving a lock's moving bolt or latch
Protective or decorative plate around a keyhole or handle
Shaped entrance passage for the matching key in a lock
Matching small metal tool used to operate many locks
Sliding fastening piece extending from a door into its frame
Round hand control used to turn a door mechanism
Vertical side of the frame receiving the door's fastening
Flat metal fitting around or behind door hardware
Device securing a door against ordinary opening
To rotate the key or handle
Hinged fastening loop commonly used with a padlock
Round lock assembly into which many keys are inserted

answerNotes.DEADBOLT: A deadbolt is moved positively by its control rather than simply retracting against a spring-loaded sloping latch face.
answerNotes.LATCH: A latch and a deadbolt perform related fastening roles but have different common mechanisms.
answerNotes.STRIKE: The strike is on the frame, while the moving fastening piece is on the door.
answerNotes.ESCUTCHEON: Escutcheon names surrounding trim, not the internal locking mechanism.
answerNotes.KEYWAY: A keyway is an opening in the lock, distinct from the decorative plate around it.

title: Inside an Upholstered Armchair
description: Look beneath an armchair’s soft covering through its padding, frame, and finishing edges.
cardDescription: Look beneath an armchair’s soft covering through its padding, frame, and finishing edges.
focus: Upholstery combines a supporting structure with padding and a cover. The clues distinguish the outer fabric from the webbing and cushioning layers below it.
solvingTip: Use the layer or body location described before choosing a textile term.
words: Padding and covering work applied to furniture
Soft padded support on an armchair's seat or back
Strong bands forming support beneath some chair padding
Raised covered cord finishing an upholstered seam
Soft sheetlike padding layer beneath a furniture cover
Small nail securing fabric or webbing to a furniture frame
Side support for an armchair sitter's forearm
Part of the chair supporting the sitter's weight
Upright support behind a seated person
Rigid structure beneath the armchair's padding
Resilient metal component supporting some upholstered seats
Cloth forming the visible chair covering
Spongy material used for many furniture cushions
Stitched join between pieces of upholstery cloth
Fabric panel hanging below the chair's main upholstered body

answerNotes.UPHOLSTERY: Upholstery includes more than the visible cloth; supporting and cushioning materials contribute to the finished seat.
answerNotes.CUSHION: A cushion contains padding within a cover, while the chair's frame supplies the rigid structure.
answerNotes.WEBBING: Webbing spans the frame in many traditional seats; it differs from the outer decorative fabric.
answerNotes.WELT: A welt defines an edge or seam; the cord is enclosed by a covering strip.
answerNotes.BATTING: Batting smooths or cushions the surface between other stuffing materials and the cover.
answerNotes.TACK: A tack fastens material mechanically rather than bonding it with glue.

title: A Cabinet Door and Drawer
description: Explore cabinet construction through frame pieces, joints, and the hardware that moves a drawer.
cardDescription: Explore cabinet construction through frame pieces, joints, and the hardware that moves a drawer.
focus: A frame-and-panel door has named vertical and horizontal members. Drawer guides and handles serve different purposes from the wood joints holding the structure together.
solvingTip: Use direction and location: upright frame piece, crosspiece, edge recess, or pulling handle.
words: Joint allowing a cabinet door to swing open
Vertical member of a frame-and-panel cabinet door
Horizontal member of a framed cabinet door
Rectangular groove cut across a board to receive another piece
Step-shaped recess cut along the edge of a board
Broad central piece enclosed by a cabinet door's frame
Small rounded handle used to pull a drawer
Horizontal board supporting objects inside a cabinet
Guide or support along which a drawer slides
Handle grasped to open a cabinet door or drawer
Hinged front closure of a cupboard
Broad flat surface of a board
Small pin used to support a movable cabinet shelf

answerNotes.HINGE: A hinge permits rotation, while a drawer runner supports sliding movement.
answerNotes.STILE: Stiles run vertically, while rails form the horizontal members.
answerNotes.RAIL: Rail has a woodworking meaning here rather than naming railway track.
answerNotes.DADO: A dado commonly runs across the grain; a rabbet is an open-sided recess along an edge.
answerNotes.RABBET: A rabbet is open to the board's edge, unlike a groove enclosed on both sides.

title: Looking at a Handwoven Rug
description: Explore a woven floor covering through its thread directions, raised surface, and finished edges.
cardDescription: Explore a woven floor covering through its thread directions, raised surface, and finished edges.
focus: Weaving crosses lengthwise and crosswise strands, while some rugs add a raised pile. A flatwoven surface and a pile surface are different structures rather than just different colors.
solvingTip: Separate the direction of a strand from the texture or edge formed by the finished work.
words: Raised surface made of loops or cut fibers on some rugs
Lengthwise strands held under tension during weaving
Crosswise strand interlaced through a rug's lengthwise threads
Finished lengthwise edge of woven material
Rug construction without an upright pile layer
Tied fastening used to form pile in many rugs
Loose thread ends extending from a rug's boundary
Small bunch of fibers projecting from a textile backing
Sheep-derived fiber used in many woven rugs
Plant fiber used for some rug strands or foundations
Decorative outer band around a rug's design
Frame or machine holding threads for weaving
Reverse side of the rug beneath its visible surface
Single line of repeated weaving or knotting

answerNotes.PILE: Pile describes the raised textile surface; a flatwoven rug does not have the same upright layer.
answerNotes.WARP: Warp forms the supported lengthwise set, while weft passes across it.
answerNotes.WEFT: Weft runs across the warp; the two directions have different names even when the fibers match.
answerNotes.SELVAGE: A selvage forms along the side during weaving, distinct from a cut end finished afterward.
answerNotes.FLATWEAVE: Flatweave describes structure rather than one national style or fiber material.
